excerpt: Figure 3 shows a weighted flow graph which represents a loop program. The count of basic blocks {A, B, C, D, E, F} are {100,90,10,0,90,100}, respectively. The arc-count of {A —+ B, A —+ C, B D, B E,C —* F, D —> F, E —> F, F —>A} are {90,10,0,90,10,0,90,99}, respectively. Clearly, the most frequently executed path in this example is the basic block sequence < A ,B ,E ,F >.
overview: The example gives a concrete mechanism for the paper's central optimization strategy: profile counts identify a path that is much hotter than nearby alternatives. Because the hot path executes far more often than the cold blocks, later transformations can trade occasional cold-path cost for lower hot-path cost without relying only on conservative static loop structure.
title: Weighted Flow Graph Counts
